articleTitle: Real time analysis of fetal phonography signals using the TMS320
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The authors describe the design of a system for real time analysis of fetal phonography signals, based on the Texas Instruments TMS320 DSP chip. It is intended that this design will form the basis of a real-time fetal monitor for use in clinical trials. The data capture requirements are assessed, and the hardware design discussed. Algorithms have been developed for determination of heart rate, and these will be extended to include detection of fetal breathing and other fetal heart sounds.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of data compression using neural networks and principal component analysis (of pulmonary scintigrams)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: PCA analysis is similar to neural networks in data compression of segments that have been 'seen', but is superior in compressing 'unseen' images. The difference between 'seen' and 'unseen' images with respect to tsse (total sum square error) is more pronounced in 32 by 16 pixel segments than 8 by 8 segments in PCA compression. This suggests that the dimensional reduction is more consistent in the smaller segments. However the tsse is lower for 'seen' segments in the larger segment PCs. Artificial neural networks also seem to generalise less readily on larger segments. Since the time taken for neural network compression is about an order of magnitude higher than PCA, and PCA is more repeatable in terms of the error magnitude, and produces lower error for 'unseen' segments, it would seem preferable to use PCA analysis than neural network methods to produce the reduced dimensional input to a diagnostic network.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Digital signal processing of the visual evoked cortical potential-survey and future directions
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The authors review the major signal processing techniques which have been developed to obtain reliable estimates of the VECP. A mathematical model for the VECP is developed. This model clearly states the general assumptions made with single VECP recordings. The major signal processing techniques used for VECP estimation are then reviewed. These techniques include Ensemble Averaging, Cross-Correlation Averaging, a posteriori 'Wiener' Filtering and Latency Corrected Averaging. Future directions are considered, including a new technique employing time-variant spectrum estimation methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measuring the shape of the mouth using structured light
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The authors have shown that colour coded light is a powerful tool for the determination of three-dimensional dental structure. The necessary algorithms for determining shape from colour coded light are described and a photography is given showing the reconstructed region which has been artificially lit by the computer and superimposed on the original image.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Use of a database to develop algorithms for ambulatory blood pressure measurement
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The author describes how the Oxford Mediloy ABP was developed and its performance verified. The database was created according to the AAMI protocol. Computer modelling of the ABP was used to develop and test the algorithms for it.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Real-time, non-invasive detection of His-Purkinje system electrograms on a beat-to-beat basis
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: A system which employs an adaptive filtering technique to analyze the HPS signal on a beat-to-beat basis has been developed. This system requires the signal to be recorded on to tape first and subsequently analyzed using the LMS adaptive algorithm. It has been found that by using this technique, valuable information about microvolt signals of clinical interest can be obtained on a beat-to-beat basis. The authors describe development of this approach and present some clinical results to demonstrate the operation of the currently available system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge based decomposition of myoelectric signals
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The authors present research relating to the use of computers for the intelligent decomposition of myoelectric signals. Digital filtering algorithms are used to reduce the noise in the signal. A normalisation and compression of the filtered signal is then performed to reduce the time of the analysis. The individual motor unit action potentials (MUAPs) in the myoelectric signal are identified using a pattern recognition method. The method uses features to describe the MUAPs in the myoelectric signal. Diagonal factor analysis is used to form uncorrelated factors from these features. The factors are then used in an adaptive clustering technique that groups together MUAPs from the same motor unit. A method is proposed whereby the superimposed waveforms formed by a summation of overlapping MUAPs are decomposed using a knowledge based expert system. Initially, a template matching procedure is used to identify the possible MUAPs that make up the superimposed waveform. The motor unit firing times are then analysed by the expert system to decide which combination of MUAPs is most probable. Rules are used in the decision making of the system and are driven by an interpreter that incorporates uncertain reasoning based on fuzzy set theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical impedance tomography (using digital signal processing)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques have been applied to the demodulators used in an EIT system and the resulting improvement in SNR has enabled data collection at real time rates. DSP technology also finds application in the real-time reconstruction of EIT images, although other processors such as the transputer are also suitable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Portable real time processing of small electrical signals from the heart
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The aim of the authors' work is to build an instrument which can be used by an Electrophysiological Measurement Technician at the patient's bedside to detect, display and record Sinus Node potentials, His bundle potentials and Ventricular Late Potentials.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A telephonic lipreading device for the hearing impaired
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The authors discuss the design of a pattern recognition system to extract appropriate lip-shapes from a speech waveform where no other cues are available. The principle of the system depends on there being an intimate relationship between lip-shapes and the corresponding state of the vocal tract. Because of this association at the articulatory level, it is believed that many of the problems associated with speech recognition systems are avoided in this instance. Careful consideration of the training procedures has been required, because of the problem of storing large amounts of visual and spoken data. The self organising property of the Kohonen map was seen as a key feature of the system design. In addition, the use of linear prediction in the pre-processor stage ensures that the data presented to the pattern recogniser is representative of those features of the vocal tract relevant to the association with the lip-shape. The design of archetypal lip-shapes has been presented and may be seen as a quantisation of the visual speech domain.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ultrasound imaging arrays for dermatological applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Biomedical Applications of Digital Signal Processing
abstract: The authors discuss the design of prototype imaging systems based on both linear and phased array concepts. Further work will lead to a new real time skin imaging system using digital signal processing techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
